brief:
Israel has become a key intermediary through which the United States channels military power and weapons into regions where Washington seeks influence without direct involvement, according to Mondoweiss. The arrangement allows the U.S. to maintain strategic reach in areas where direct American military presence would prove politically complicated or diplomatically costly.

The relationship reflects decades of military coordination between the two countries. Israel's role as an arms intermediary extends U.S. geopolitical interests across multiple regions, enabling Washington to pursue objectives through a proxy partner while maintaining plausible distance from direct operations.
dek: In episode three of The Necessary State, Sana Saeed traces how Israel became one of America’s most useful intermediaries, carrying U.S. military power, weapons, and influence into places where Washington wants a foothold without direct involvement.
title: Israel serves as U.S. intermediary for weapons exports to restricted nations
